subject: Ancient & Culture
q: With reference to the history of ancient India, Bhavabhuti, Hastimalla and Kshemeshvara were famous:
exp: Bhavabhuti (Malatimadhava), Hastimalla, and Kshemeshvara were renowned Sanskrit/Prakrit playwrights.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: Which of the following Harappan sites is famous for its dockyard?
exp: Lothal in Gujarat was a major port town of the Indus Valley Civilization known for its brick-built tidal dockyard.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: The famous 'Great Bath' was discovered at which Indus Valley site?
exp: The Great Bath, a watertight baked-brick tank likely used for ritual bathing, was excavated at Mohenjo-daro.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: In which rock edict did Ashoka mention the Kalinga War and his remorse over the bloodshed?
exp: Major Rock Edict XIII records Ashoka's victory over Kalinga, his deep remorse, and his turn towards Dhamma-vijaya.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: The 'Ajanta Caves' in Maharashtra are primarily associated with which religion?
exp: All 29–30 rock-cut caves at Ajanta are exclusively Buddhist (Hinayana and Mahayana phases), famous for Jataka mural paintings.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: Who authored the Sanskrit play 'Mudrarakshasa', which narrates the ascent of Chandragupta Maurya?
exp: Vishakhadatta wrote Mudrarakshasa during the Gupta period, depicting Chanakya's political strategies for Chandragupta Maurya.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: In medieval Indian history, the 'Iqtadari System' was institutionalized by:
exp: Shams-ud-din Iltutmish organized the Iqta system, assigning land revenue rights to nobles (Iqtadars) in lieu of cash salaries.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: The 'Brihadisvara Temple' at Thanjavur was built by which Chola ruler?
exp: Built by Rajaraja Chola I around 1010 CE, the Brihadisvara Temple is a pinnacle of Dravida temple architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: Which Bhakti saint was a disciple of Ramananda and composed verses included in the Guru Granth Sahib?
exp: Kabir, a nirguna Bhakti saint and disciple of Ramananda, rejected ritualism and caste; over 500 of his verses appear in the Guru Granth Sahib.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: The 'Sattriya' classical dance form originated in which Indian state?
exp: Sattriya was introduced in the 15th century by Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev in the monasteries (Sattras) of Assam.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: The 'Mansabdari System' introduced by Akbar was primarily a system of:
options: Grading military and civil nobility by rank (Zat and Sawar)
exp: Under the Mansabdari system, every officer held a Mansab (rank) comprising Zat (personal status/salary) and Sawar (cavalry quota to maintain).

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: Which of the following Buddhist Councils was held at Kundalavana in Kashmir under the patronage of Kanishka?
exp: The Fourth Buddhist Council (1st century CE) was presided over by Vasumitra under Kushana emperor Kanishka, marking the formal Mahayana-Hinayana division.

subject: Ancient & Culture
q: The 'Gandhara School of Art' flourished under the Kushanas and was heavily influenced by:
exp: Gandhara art blended Buddhist themes with Greco-Roman realism (wavy hair, muscular drapery, grey-bluish schist stone).
